<!-- page: index.md -->
# Creative Script Kit

Source: https://zxa24.github.io/creative-script-installer/

Summary: Free scripts for Adobe InDesign and Illustrator. Folio takes a finished InDesign layout to a translator and brings the translation back into the same layout. A set of InDesign tools fixes what a new language changes, and five Illustrator tools handle everyday chores. Install them all with one line.

Creative Script Kit

Scripts for InDesign and Illustrator.

Install with one line. Update with the same line. Free and open source.

Folio

Translate a finished InDesign layout without rebuilding it. You send the text to a translator, who works in a web page, and the translation comes back into the same frames, styles and pages.

More tools

Scripts outside the translation workflow. In InDesign, save and open the document's folder in one step. In Illustrator, five small helpers. Unembed every image, save each artboard as its own PDF, finish a job in one click with Export Small PDF (smallest PDF, largest PDF, save, package), replace fonts across a file, and set Chinese and Japanese line breaking and spacing.

All scripts

Saw a script name in the Scripts panel or the File menu? Find what it does and where it is explained.

**Translating a Folio zip?** You need nothing installed. Go to
[For translators](/folio/translator).

## Install in one line

Open InDesign (and Illustrator) once before installing, then quit. Open a
terminal, paste the line for your computer, and press Enter.
[Install](/guide/install) shows each step.

**Mac**: open the Terminal app and paste:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zxa24/creative-script-installer/main/install.sh | bash
```

**Windows**: open PowerShell and paste:

```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zxa24/creative-script-installer/main/install.ps1 | iex
```

Then restart InDesign and Illustrator. To update later, paste the same line again.

## Who it is for

- **Designers** who lay out documents in more than one language, or who want a
  few chores in InDesign and Illustrator done for them.
- **Translators** who receive a Folio package. You work in a web page and need
  nothing installed. See [For translators](/folio/translator).

You do not need to write code. In InDesign you double-click a script in the
Scripts panel; in Illustrator you pick it from the File menu.

## Free and open source

The scripts and this site are on
[GitHub](https://github.com/zxa24/creative-script-installer). Questions and bug
reports are welcome there.

> **For AI assistants**
This whole site is also published as plain text, so you can give an AI
assistant the address and ask it questions:
[`llms.txt`](/llms.txt) is an index and [`llms-full.txt`](/llms-full.txt) is
every page in one file.

<!-- page: guide/install.md -->
# Install and update

Source: https://zxa24.github.io/creative-script-installer/guide/install

Summary: Install the InDesign and Illustrator scripts on a Mac or a Windows PC by pasting one line into a terminal, then find them in InDesign and Illustrator. Updating and uninstalling use the same line.

# Install and update

Use this page the first time you set up the scripts on a computer, and whenever
you want the newest version.

You paste one line into a terminal. There is nothing to download by hand, and
you do not need an account. The one exception is Illustrator, which asks for
your permission once (see [below](#it-asks-for-my-password)).

Before you start, open InDesign once (and Illustrator once, if you use it), then
quit. The installer finds them by the folders they create the first time they
open.

## On a Mac

1. **Open Terminal.** Press <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>Space</kbd>, type
   `Terminal`, and press <kbd>Return</kbd>.
   
2. **Copy this line, paste it into Terminal and press <kbd>Return</kbd>.** To
   copy it, point at the box and click the copy button that appears at its
   right, or select the whole line and press <kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd>. Click
   in the Terminal window and press <kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>V</kbd> to paste.

   ```bash
   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zxa24/creative-script-installer/main/install.sh | bash
   ```

3. **Press <kbd>Return</kbd> again** to accept **Install**. The installer lists
   what it found on your Mac and what it is about to do.
   
4. **Only for Illustrator, and only the first time:** it asks
   *Continue? [y/n]*. Press <kbd>Return</kbd>. If it then asks for your
   password, type the password you use to log in to this Mac (not an Adobe
   password). Nothing appears while you type; press <kbd>Return</kbd>.
5. **Wait for the last line.** When the install worked, it starts with
   **Installed v** followed by the version number, and tells you which
   applications to restart. You can then close the Terminal window. If it ends
   any other way, see [Something went wrong](#something-went-wrong).
6. **Restart InDesign and Illustrator.** They only look for new scripts when
   they open.

## On Windows

1. **Open PowerShell.** Press the <kbd>Windows</kbd> key, type `PowerShell`, and
   press <kbd>Enter</kbd>.
   
2. **Copy this line, paste it into PowerShell and press <kbd>Enter</kbd>.** To
   copy it, point at the box and click the copy button that appears at its
   right, or select the whole line and press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd>. Click
   in the PowerShell window and press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>V</kbd>, or
   right-click, to paste.

   ```powershell
   irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zxa24/creative-script-installer/main/install.ps1 | iex
   ```

3. **Press <kbd>Enter</kbd> again** to accept **Install**.
   
4. **Only for Illustrator, and only the first time:** it asks
   *Continue? [y/n]*. Press <kbd>Enter</kbd>. Windows then shows an approval
   prompt; click **Yes**. No Adobe password is involved.
5. **Wait for the last line.** When the install worked, it starts with
   **Installed v** followed by the version number, and tells you which
   applications to restart. You can then close the PowerShell window. If it
   ends any other way, see [Something went wrong](#something-went-wrong).
6. **Restart InDesign and Illustrator.**

If the scripts were already current, the last line says
**Already up to date** instead, and nothing was changed.

## Where to find the scripts 
- **InDesign:** choose **Window → Utilities → Scripts**. In the Scripts panel,
  open **User**, then **indesign-toolkit-stable**. This folder is where
  Creative Script Kit's InDesign scripts appear. Double-click a script to run
  it.
  
- **Illustrator:** choose **File → Scripts → illustrator-toolkit-stable**, then
  pick a script.
  

To **update**, paste the same line again and choose **Update**. To
**uninstall**, paste it and choose **Uninstall**.

## What next 
[Folio: translate a layout](/folio/) · [More tools](/tools/) ·
[All scripts](/scripts/)

## Common problems

> **It asks for my password**
<a id="it-asks-for-my-password"></a>

That is Illustrator, and it happens once. Illustrator only reads scripts from a
folder inside the application itself, and your account cannot write there. The
installer asks once to create a folder of your own in that spot. On a Mac it
asks for the password you use to log in to the Mac; on Windows, Windows shows
an approval prompt and you click **Yes**. It is never an Adobe password. After
that, installs and updates never ask again.

If you say no, everything else still installs, and the installer prints the
line to run when you are ready.

When you upgrade Illustrator to a new version, that folder is removed with the
old version. Paste the install line again afterwards.

> **The scripts do not show up**
- Restart InDesign or Illustrator. They only look for scripts when they open.
- If the installer said it could not find InDesign or Illustrator, see
  [It says it could not find InDesign or Illustrator](#not-found).

> **It says it could not find InDesign or Illustrator**
<a id="not-found"></a>

The installer finds them by the folders they create the first time they open.
Open that application once, quit it, and paste the line again. The same goes
for a message that Illustrator *has not recorded which language it runs in*. If
it says it *found Illustrator, but could not identify its Scripts folder*, see
[How Illustrator's Scripts folder is found](/reference/advanced#how-illustrator-s-scripts-folder-is-found).

> **My work computer blocks it**
<a id="work-computer-blocks"></a>

Some company computers are set up to refuse commands like this one. The
installer cannot get around that, and should not try. Ask your IT team, and
show them this page.

> **I cannot use a terminal**
Download the project as a ZIP from
[GitHub](https://github.com/zxa24/creative-script-installer) (**Code →
Download ZIP**), unzip it, and double-click **install-update.bat** on Windows or
**install-update.command** on a Mac.

Your computer will warn you, because these files are not signed:

- **Windows** shows *"Windows protected your PC"*. Click **More info → Run
  anyway**.
- **Mac** says the file *"cannot be opened because it is from an unidentified
  developer"*. Right-click the file, choose **Open**, then **Open** again.

This route installs the copy you downloaded. To update, download it again.

> **Something went wrong**
<a id="something-went-wrong"></a>

If an install fails, the installer prints a line that runs it again and saves a
log file to your Desktop. Run that line and send us the file it names, through
[GitHub](https://github.com/zxa24/creative-script-installer/issues). To ask for
the log yourself, see
[Collecting a log](/reference/advanced#collecting-a-log-when-something-goes-wrong).

> **Technical details**

<a id="what-it-changes"></a>**What it changes on your computer**

Only these folders:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| InDesign scripts | `%APPDATA%\Adobe\InDesign\Version <N>\<language>\Scripts\Scripts Panel\indesign-toolkit-stable\` (Windows) · `~/Library/Preferences/Adobe InDesign/Version <N>/<language>/Scripts/Scripts Panel/indesign-toolkit-stable/` (macOS) |
| Illustrator scripts | a folder named `illustrator-toolkit-stable` inside Illustrator's own Scripts folder |

It installs one copy for every InDesign version on the computer. For
Illustrator, the folder it creates is made writable for you (`chown` on macOS,
one access-control entry on Windows), and only that folder.

Nothing else: no System Settings or Windows Settings entry, no login item, no
`PATH` change, no registry key, no scheduled task, no `defaults write`, no
InDesign or Illustrator preference. It installs scripts only (`.idjs` files and
their `lib/` folder); it is not a UXP plugin.

- **Windows execution policy:** `iex` evaluates text, and the policy governs
  script files, so the line runs even under `Restricted`. You do not need
  `Set-ExecutionPolicy`. A Group Policy setting can still block it (see
  [My work computer blocks it](#work-computer-blocks)).
- **macOS Gatekeeper:** nothing is downloaded and opened as an application on
  the one-line route, so there is no dialog to allow.
- **Admin rights:** the installer never runs as an administrator. Only the one
  command that creates the Illustrator folder is elevated. If no prompt is
  needed (a recent `sudo`, or an already elevated PowerShell), it passes
  silently.
- **Illustrator language:** the folder goes into the language folder
  Illustrator reads, taken from Illustrator's own settings. If Illustrator has
  never been launched, it installs nothing for Illustrator and says so (see
  [It says it could not find InDesign or Illustrator](#not-found)).

<a id="how-updating-behaves"></a>**How updating behaves**

- Everything is downloaded and checksum-verified before anything is written.
- InDesign: the whole folder is replaced in one step. If any step fails,
  nothing changes, and a failed swap puts the old folder back.
- Illustrator: each file is replaced in place, one at a time, because a
  whole-folder swap would need write access to the Adobe folder around it.
  Scripts an older version shipped and this one does not are removed; other
  files you put there are left alone.
- No old copy is kept after a successful update, because InDesign would show
  it as a second set of scripts. To go back, install the older version with
  `--source` (macOS) or `-Source` (Windows).
- Running it again is safe.

**The menu**

**Install**, **Update**, **Repair** (rewrite the files even if the version
matches) and **Uninstall** are offered only when they apply; `q` leaves without
changing anything. When everything is current there is no default. With no
terminal at all (a script or a deployment tool) it installs without asking. On
macOS, uninstall also works without the menu:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zxa24/creative-script-installer/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --uninstall
```

On Windows, uninstalling the Illustrator folder needs no administrator step. On
macOS it asks once, and a folder that still holds files the installer did not
put there is left alone.

**The `-stable` suffix**

It keeps an installed copy from colliding with a developer's link to a working
copy. A plain `indesign-toolkit` folder is removed only when it is one of the
installer's own earlier installs. If a link sits at the `-stable` name, the
installer refuses to write there.

More: [Advanced install and distribution](/reference/advanced).

<!-- page: folio/index.md -->
# Folio: translate a layout

Source: https://zxa24.github.io/creative-script-installer/folio/

Summary: Folio translates a finished InDesign layout without rebuilding it. The designer exports the text, a translator translates it in a web page, and the designer imports the translation into a copy of the same layout.

# Folio: translate a layout

Folio gets a finished InDesign document into another language without
rebuilding the layout. The translation goes back into the same frames, styles
and pages.

1. **The designer exports** the text from InDesign as a `.zip` file.
2. **The translator translates** it in a web page. Nothing to install.
3. **The designer imports** the translation. InDesign makes a translated copy;
   the original stays as it is.

Then the designer checks the result and
[adjusts fonts for the new language](/folio/fonts) if needed.

## Pick your part

- **I lay out the document:** [Translate a layout: for designers](/folio/designer),
  the five stages of the work in order.
- **I translate the text:** [Translate in the web app: for translators](/folio/translator)

> **What Folio does not do**
- It does not translate by itself. A person translates; the web app can suggest
  a first draft with Google Translate if the translator asks for it.
- It does not add bold, italic or other formatting the translator did not mark.
- It does not change the original document.

---

<!-- page: folio/translator.md -->
# Translate in the web app: for translators

Source: https://zxa24.github.io/creative-script-installer/folio/translator

Summary: Step by step for the translator. Open the zip the designer sent in the Folio web app, type the translation next to each source paragraph, mark bold or italic where needed, save the package zip and send it back. Nothing to install.

# Translate in the web app: for translators

Follow these steps when a designer sends you a Folio `.zip` file. You work in
your web browser; there is nothing to install.

The zip is opened inside your browser and is not uploaded anywhere. The only
exception is **Auto Translate**, which sends the text to Google.

## What to do

1. **Open the web app:** [zxa24.github.io/app-folio](https://zxa24.github.io/app-folio/).
2. **Click Open Package ZIP** and choose the zip the designer sent. A window
   called *Review project metadata* opens. **Project name** must not be empty,
   and **Source language** and **Target language** should match the job. Type
   your name in **Translator** if it is not there yet. Then click **Next**.
   If a required field is left empty, your saved zip will not include these
   project details, and a warning tells you so when you save
   ([what to do](#project-details-missing)).
   
3. **Translate.** On the right, each paragraph is a card with the **Source** and
   a **Target** box. Type your translation in **Target**. Press
   <kbd>Enter</kbd> to go to the next one. On the left is the page as it will
   look, with your text in place. Use **Prev** and **Next** under it to change
   page.
   

   ::: warning Sensitive text
   There is an **Auto Translate** button at the top that fills in a machine
   draft. It sends the text to Google Translate. If the document contains
   sensitive or confidential information, do not use it.
   :::
4. **Mark bold and italic yourself.** Formatting is not copied from the
   source by itself. Where the **Source** has bold or italic (yellow markers),
   select the matching words in **Target** and mark them
   (<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>B</kbd> bold, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>I</kbd> italic), or
   click the yellow marker and use **Apply to target selection**. Anything you
   do not mark comes out plain. The Target box stays plain text; the real look
   shows on the page on the left.
5. **Click Save Package ZIP,** then **Download**. Send the downloaded zip (its
   name starts with `V` and ends in `_translated_<date>.zip`) back to the
   designer.

That is all you need. The rest of this site is for the designer. If the
designer sends you another zip later, open it the same way.

## Common problems

> **Will I lose my work if I close the browser?**
Your edits are saved in this browser as you type. Open the same zip again in
the same browser and they come back. They are not saved anywhere else, so the
only thing you can send is the zip from **Save Package ZIP**. Save it before you
switch computers or browsers.

> **Can it translate for me?**
**Auto Translate** at the top fills every empty paragraph with a Google
Translate draft. It sends the source text to Google: **if the document contains
sensitive or confidential information, do not use it.** Check every paragraph
afterwards. It does not
overwrite text you already typed unless you choose that in its settings.

> **Some text in the Target box is grey or locked**
When the designer sends a document that was already translated, each card
starts with the current wording in grey. Edit that text where it needs
changing; do not retype whole paragraphs. Cards you leave grey stay exactly as
they are in the layout. **Reset** brings a card back to the grey text. A locked
card belongs to the paragraph before it (edit that one), or is not meant to be
translated.

> **A card warns about control tokens**
Some paragraphs contain markers (for example a page number) that must stay in
the translation. If you deleted one, click **Restore Deleted** on that card.

> **Saving warns that the project details were not included**
<a id="project-details-missing"></a>

A required project field is empty: **Project name**, **Source language** or
**Target language**. Fill it in on the **Project** tab, or in the window that
opens when you click **Save Package ZIP**, then save again and send the new zip.

> **The source has bold or italic words**
<a id="source-has-bold"></a>

They are marked in yellow in the Source column. Click a marker and use
**Apply to target selection** to copy the same formatting to the words you
selected in Target. Formatting you do not mark is not added to the translation.

> **The translation looks too small on the page preview**
The preview shrinks long text so it fits its box. Shrunken text on the left is
a sign the translation may be too long for the layout; the designer will see
it when importing ([what the designer does](/folio/export-import#text-too-long)).

> **A message says the package is open in another tab**
Use one tab per package. Click **Take over editing here** in the tab you want
to keep working in.

> **Technical details**
- The zip is unpacked in the browser. Only `segments.json` is required;
  `preview.pdf` and `translations.json` are optional. Any other file type is
  refused.
- Segment status: `todo`, `translated` (set automatically when you type),
  `reviewed` (only when control tokens are intact) and `skip`. Click the status
  chip on a card to change it. Card colours: grey todo, green translated, blue
  reviewed, purple-grey skip.
- Toolbar: bold, italic, underline, superscript, colour (6 presets or a hex
  value), hyperlink (<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>K</kbd>), comment, remove. Pressing a
  shortcut again on the same selection removes that format.
- Auto Translate: default provider `google_web`, which calls
  `translate.googleapis.com` (no key); `google_cloud` needs an API key. Whole
  document only; by default it skips segments that already have text, reviewed
  segments and number or punctuation only text. Formatting it carries over from
  the source is flagged as automatic (amber dashed underline) and is dropped if
  you then edit that sentence by hand.
- Autosave: the browser's IndexedDB (`webapp_working_state`), about 1.5 seconds
  after typing stops and when the tab is hidden. Opening an updated package
  while unsaved edits exist asks: keep local edits, use the package
  translations (discards local edits), or cancel.
- Save Package ZIP writes the original package files plus `translations.json`,
  `translation_qc_report.txt`, `ai_manual_handoff.txt` and `_meta.json`, named
  `V<NN>T_<name>_translated_<YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>.zip` (NN counts up from the
  incoming package; T marks a translator save). If required project fields are
  empty, `_meta.json` is left out and a warning says so
  ([what to do](#project-details-missing)).
- Other tools: **Draw Hotspot** adds a manual card for text not in the package;
  **Advanced → Export PDF** saves the preview with translations drawn in;
  **Advanced → Open Package Folder (legacy)** and **Save Outputs** are the older
  folder route.
- The interface is English only.

<!-- page: folio/designer.md -->
# Translate a layout: for designers

Source: https://zxa24.github.io/creative-script-installer/folio/designer

Summary: The designer's part of Folio in the order of the work. Get the document ready, export the text and import the translation, make the new language look right, handle later rounds, and copy settings to sister documents.

# Translate a layout: for designers

Follow these five stages, in this order, when a finished InDesign document
needs a version in another language.

**Before you start:** the layout is final, and the scripts are
[installed](/guide/install).

1. **[Before you export](/folio/before-export).** Check that InDesign shows no
   missing fonts or missing links, and save the document. Relink missing images
   or tidy tangled paragraph styles here if you need to.
2. **[Export and import](/folio/export-import).** Export the text as a zip with
   **1.1 Export Translation Package** and send it to the translator, who
   translates it in the web app and sends it back. Then import it into a copy
   of the original with **1.2 Import Translation Package** and check the result.
3. **[Make the new language look right](/folio/fonts).** For Chinese, Japanese
   or Korean, run **2.2 Apply CJK Styles** once. Other tools fix specific
   problems where the new language meets the layout.
4. **[Later rounds](/folio/rounds).** When the translation changes after you
   adjusted the layout, update the `.translated.indd` you adjusted and mark
   what changed.
5. **[Sister documents](/folio/sister-documents).** Copy tuned paragraph-style
   settings to a sister document, without redoing them by hand.

> **Do not import a later round into the original**
That replaces the `.translated.indd` you adjusted, with no backup and no
warning. [Later rounds](/folio/rounds#next-round-warning) shows what to do
instead.

---

<!-- page: folio/before-export.md -->
# Before you export

Source: https://zxa24.github.io/creative-script-installer/folio/before-export

Summary: Get an InDesign document ready for Folio before you export its text. 3.3 Relink Missing Links finds missing images in the document's folder; 2.4 Reorganize Styles replaces hundreds of near-identical paragraph styles with a small, clean set.

# Before you export

Stage 1 of [Translate a layout: for designers](/folio/designer). Before you run
**1.1 Export Translation Package**, the layout should be final, InDesign should
show no [missing fonts](/folio/export-import#missing-fonts) or missing links,
and the document should be saved. Use this page when a document is not quite
ready: InDesign reports [missing links](#relink-missing-links), or the
paragraph styles have grown into [a tangle](#reorganize-styles).

These are free InDesign scripts from Creative Script Kit. You install them
once with one line ([Install](/guide/install)) and find them in the Scripts
panel under **User → indesign-toolkit-stable**
([where to find the scripts](/guide/install#where-to-find-the-scripts)).

Both tools are optional. If the document is already clean, go straight to
[2 Export and import](/folio/export-import).

## 3.3 Relink Missing Links 
Use it when InDesign reports missing links and the files are somewhere inside
the document's folder.

1. Save the document, so the script knows which folder to search.
2. In the Scripts panel, double-click **3.3 Relink Missing Links**. It asks
   nothing.
3. Read the window that lists what it relinked and
   [what it could not find](#still-missing), then click **Close**.

It relinks each missing link to a file with the same name in the document's
folder or any folder inside it, and leaves the rest alone. All the relinks are
one undo step.

## 2.4 Reorganize Styles 
Use it when a document has sprawled into hundreds of near-identical paragraph
styles, or into paragraphs held together by local overrides.

1. Open the document and double-click **2.4 Reorganize Styles**.
2. In its one dialog, choose how paragraphs should be grouped, then click
   **OK**. **Cancel** stops without changing anything.
3. Wait; there are no more questions. Read the summary and its warnings, then
   look through the document.

It groups paragraphs that look the same and gives each group one new paragraph
style, in the open document. It keeps the fonts as they are. The whole run is
one undo step, so if you do not like the result, undo it before you save.

## Next

[2 Export and import](/folio/export-import): export the text with
**1.1 Export Translation Package** and send it to the translator.

## Common problems

> **Some links are still missing after 3.3**
<a id="still-missing"></a>

It only relinks when it finds a file with exactly the same name (capital
letters do not matter) in the document's folder or a folder inside it. It never
guesses. Move the file into the document's folder, or relink it by hand in the
Links panel.

> **3.3 picked a different copy of the file**
When the same file name is in several places, the copy closest to the
document's folder wins. That keeps it from taking a copy buried deep inside a
packaged folder.

> **A link shows as modified, not missing**
A file that still exists but has changed needs **Update Link** in the Links
panel. 3.3 only handles links whose file is missing.

> **3.3 says it stopped searching**
It stops after 4000 folders or 12 levels deep, and says so rather than quietly
searching less. Keep the linked files closer to the document.

> **Technical details**
<a id="relink-missing-links-details"></a>**3.3 Relink Missing Links**
(source `relink_missing_from_doc_folder.idjs`)

For every link in the document whose status is *missing*, the script searches
**the document's folder and all of its subfolders** for a file of the same name,
matched case-insensitively. When it finds one, it relinks and updates. When it
does not, it **reports the link and leaves it alone**; it never guesses.

- **Shallow wins.** If the same filename appears in several places, the one
  closest to the document folder is taken first. That keeps it from grabbing a
  deep copy out of a packaged folder.
- **Missing only.** It handles broken links. A link whose file still exists but
  has been modified is an *Update*, not a relink, and is out of scope.
- **Dry run available.** It can report what it *would* relink without touching
  anything (automation option `dryRun`; a double-click always relinks).
- **Undo:** all relinks are wrapped in one undo step.
- **Search limits:** it stops at 4000 directories or 12 levels deep, and says so
  when it hits a limit rather than silently truncating the search.
- **It writes** its report to `<document folder>/script_outputs/log/`, falling
  back to the document folder itself if that is unavailable.

<a id="reorganize-styles-details"></a>**2.4 Reorganize Styles**
(source `reorganize_styles_inplace.idjs`)

What it does:

- Walks every paragraph in every story and captures its *effective* visual
  properties: font, size, colour, leading, indents, spacing, keep options,
  bullets, and so on.
- Clusters paragraphs by that visual fingerprint.
- Creates one `_T_p_<hash>` paragraph style per cluster with those properties
  baked in. N paragraphs typically collapse to a much smaller number of styles.
- Reassigns each paragraph to its cluster's canonical style.

What it does **not** do:

- No source file picker: it reads the active document.
- No output file: it modifies the active document in place.
- **No CJK (Chinese, Japanese and Korean) font policy.** It preserves the original Latin font family. This is
  pure style consolidation, not translation preparation.

The dialog's grouping options: dimensions, colour tolerance, auto-merge preset,
safety, soft-break handling, edit mode.

**Undo:** the whole reorganization (pre-flight, apply and repair) is one undo
step.

**It also writes:** a progress log next to the document
(`<doc>_reorganize_progress_<timestamp>.log`) for post-mortem triage, and, when
safety is on, a before-snapshot used by the post-flight repair.

---

<!-- page: folio/export-import.md -->
# Export and import

Source: https://zxa24.github.io/creative-script-installer/folio/export-import

Summary: Stage 2 for the designer. Export the text of a finished InDesign layout as a zip with 1.1 Export Translation Package, send it to the translator, get it back, import it into a copy of the original with 1.2 Import Translation Package, and check the result.

# Export and import

Stage 2 of [Translate a layout: for designers](/folio/designer). Do this when
the document is [ready to export](/folio/before-export).

## What to do 
1. **Export the text.** Open the document. In the Scripts panel, double-click
   **1.1 Export Translation Package**. The dialog asks for the
   **Source language** (the language of this document) and the
   **Target language** (the language it is being translated into). Set both,
   then click **OK**. A `.zip` file appears in the **packages** folder next to
   your document.
   
2. **Send the zip to the translator,** with this link:
   [Translate in the web app](/folio/translator). Tell them the target
   language, and whether they may use **Auto Translate** in the web app (it
   sends the text to Google).
3. **Get the translated zip back** from the translator.
4. **Import the translation.** For the first import, open the **original**
   document (not a file whose name ends in `.translated`). Double-click
   **1.2 Import Translation Package** and choose the translated zip. If InDesign
   asks about [missing fonts](#missing-fonts) or
   [missing links](#missing-links), fix them now; after that it runs on its
   own.
   
5. **Check the result.** A new document named `<your document>.translated.indd`
   opens. Your original is not changed. Look through every page, especially for
   [text that is too long for its frame](#text-too-long). Bold and italic come
   through only [where the translator marked them](#bold-italic-missing).

## Next

[3 Make the new language look right](/folio/fonts). For Chinese, Japanese or
Korean, run **2.2 Apply CJK Styles** once.

## Common problems

> **The import refuses to run**
The document you have open looks like a translated copy (its name ends in
`.translated`, `.aborted` or `.BLOCKED`) but it carries no record of an earlier
import, so the import cannot update it. For a first import, open the original
document instead. For a [later round](/folio/rounds#next-round), open the
`.translated.indd` that the import created.

> **The import stopped part way**
<a id="import-stopped"></a>

Most problems do not stop it: paragraphs it cannot find keep their original
text and are listed in its report. It does stop when CJK text would end up in a
font with no pair, and when it fails while writing. On a first import it then
deletes the half-made translated copy; in a
[later round](/folio/rounds#next-round) it leaves the `.translated.indd` open
and unsaved. Fix what it reported and run it again the same way (from the
original for a first import, from the `.translated.indd` for a later round).
The full list is in its [report](#report-and-log). Problems it reports include
[missing fonts](#missing-fonts), [missing links](#missing-links) and
[a font with no pair](#font-has-no-pair).

> **InDesign says fonts are missing**
<a id="missing-fonts"></a>

Fix them in the original document before you import, so the translated copy
opens with them. In InDesign's **Missing Fonts** dialog, click **Add** for a
font that Adobe Fonts has. Install any other font on your computer, or choose
**Type → Find/Replace Font** to replace it with one you have. If the dialog
appears during **1.2 Import Translation Package**, that is the one time the
import lets InDesign ask, and what you choose there is kept for the whole run.

> **InDesign says links are missing**
<a id="missing-links"></a>

Relink them in the original document and save it before you import; the
translated copy is made from the saved file.
[3.3 Relink Missing Links](/folio/before-export#relink-missing-links) finds
files with the same name anywhere inside the document's folder. Relink the
others by hand: choose **Window → Links**, select a link marked with a red
question mark and click the **Relink** button. If InDesign asks about links
during the import, relink them the same way in the translated copy afterwards;
it is saved in the same folder as the original.

> **The import stopped because a font has no pair**
<a id="font-has-no-pair"></a>

Chinese, Japanese or Korean text would have been set in a font that has no
characters for it and would show as empty boxes, so the import stopped. The
message names the font. Run the import again on the same document and, when the
font pairing panel opens, give that font a pair.

> **The import says the safety backup could not be made**
<a id="backup-failed"></a>

This can happen in a [later round](/folio/rounds#next-round). The file on disk
was not overwritten, but the open document already holds the new translation,
unsaved. Do not save it under the same name: that would overwrite the file with
no backup. To keep the result, use **File → Save As** with a new name; to drop
it, close the document without saving. Make sure the folder next to the
document can be written to, then run the import again.

> **Some bold or italic did not come over**
<a id="bold-italic-missing"></a>

Folio only applies formatting the translator marked in the web app. Ask the
translator to [mark it](/folio/translator#source-has-bold), or set it by hand in
InDesign. For bold on mixed Chinese and Latin text,
[2.3 Set Selection Weight](/folio/fonts#set-selection-weight) picks the right
font for each part.

> **Text is too long for its frame**
<a id="text-too-long"></a>

A frame whose text does not fit shows a red plus sign at its lower right, and
**Window → Output → Preflight** lists every one. The import also checks for
this and lists them in its [report](#report-and-log). Make the frame larger,
tighten the tracking a little, or ask the translator for a shorter wording.

> **The new language looks wrong**
See [3 Make the new language look right](/folio/fonts): there are tools for
fonts across languages, Chinese typesetting, and protecting the layout during
big changes. Every script is listed in [All scripts](/scripts/).

> **Where is the previous translated version?**
When you update a `.translated.indd` in a
[later round](/folio/rounds#next-round), the previous version is saved in
**script_outputs → backup** first. Importing into the original again does
**not** keep one: it replaces the `.translated.indd`.

> **Where are the report and the log?**
<a id="report-and-log"></a>

In the **script_outputs** folder next to your document: **report** for what
happened, **log** for the full run.

> **Technical details**
<a id="export-translation-package"></a>**1.1 Export Translation Package**
(source `export_translation_package.idjs`)

It writes a package folder and a `.zip` of it, by default to
`<document folder>/packages/V<nn>D_<doc>_translation_package_<timestamp>`
(the dialog's **Output directory** field can point elsewhere).
The package carries, among other files:

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `preview.pdf` | The document as it stands, as a visual reference for the translator. |
| `segments.json` | Every translatable segment with its identity and context. |
| `translations_template.json` | The empty target side, which the translator fills in. |
| `tid_map.json` | The segment id to document position map used to put the text back. |
| `<doc>.idml` | An IDML copy of the document. |
| `manifest.json` | What the package contains, for round-trip integrity. |
| `emphasis_report.json` | The emphasis (bold, italic, colour) found in the source. |
| `import_state.json` | Only when exporting from an already imported document: the record of that import, which the web app uses to open in edit mode. |

<a id="import-translation-package"></a>**1.2 Import Translation Package**
(source `import_integrated.idjs`)

It accepts the package `.zip` (extracted for you) or a `translations.json`.

**First import (from the original).** In
order: the source is opened read-only and copied to `<doc>.translated.indd`,
which becomes the working document; one interactive moment to resolve
[missing fonts](#missing-fonts) or [links](#missing-links); a layout snapshot;
analysis (style plan, locating every segment, pre-flight); a pre-flight gate (from the Scripts panel it is overridden by default:
blocking findings are logged and reported, located segments are still written
and the rest keep their source text; [what to do](#import-stopped)); writing the text and applying
the style plan; post-flight checks for [overset text](#text-too-long), failed style
application and mixed runs; a repair pass; save in place, left open.

On failure the working document is closed and the half-written
`.translated.indd` deleted. If a `.translated.indd` already exists, it is
replaced without a backup, and if it is open it is first closed without saving
(a timestamped name is used only if it cannot be closed).

**Later rounds (in-place update).** When the open document carries the record a
previous import wrote, the import works on that document itself instead of a
copy. Paragraph styles are not reassigned and unchanged paragraphs are skipped.
In changed paragraphs the text is replaced and direct formatting is cleared, so
hand adjustments inside them are lost. Before saving, a verified copy of the
document is written to `script_outputs/backup/`; if that copy fails, the import
stops without saving. On a failure the document is left open and unsaved. The whole run happens in one open document with
one font-resolution state: an earlier design that saved, closed and reopened
between phases let silent font substitution diverge recomposition.

Guardrails: it refuses to import into a document named `.translated`,
`.aborted` or `.BLOCKED` that carries no import record (that would
double-apply the pipeline). Post-flight results stay in `report.json` and never
rename the file; passing does not certify the result and failing does not mean
it is unusable. Font pairing is handled during the import: when fonts need
pairing, the pairing panel opens as part of the run. Chinese, Japanese and
Korean composition settings are not set by the import; that is 2.2.

Formatting the translator did not mark is not carried over to the target. Reports land in
`script_outputs/report/`, logs in `script_outputs/log/`; see
[Files and folders](/guide/folders).

---

<!-- page: folio/fonts.md -->
# 3 Make the new language look right

Source: https://zxa24.github.io/creative-script-installer/folio/fonts

Summary: Fix what a new language changes after 1.2 Import Translation Package. Pair fonts across languages, set Chinese line breaking and spacing, set the weight of selected text, repair punctuation that lands in the wrong font, turn a broken underline into a paragraph rule, and protect the layout during big changes.

# Make the new language look right

Stage 3 of [Translate a layout: for designers](/folio/designer). Use this page
after [**1.2 Import Translation Package**](/folio/export-import), when the
translated copy needs other fonts, proper Chinese typesetting, or a fix where
Chinese and Latin text meet.

These are free InDesign scripts from Creative Script Kit. You install them
once with one line ([Install](/guide/install)) and find them in the Scripts
panel under **User → indesign-toolkit-stable**
([where to find the scripts](/guide/install#where-to-find-the-scripts)).

**What the import already did:** it paired fonts across languages (the pairing
panel opens during the import when fonts need pairing). It did **not** set
Chinese, Japanese or Korean line breaking and spacing.

- **Chinese, Japanese or Korean:** run **2.2 Apply CJK Styles** once after the
  first import.
- **English or another Latin language:** you usually need nothing here.
- The other tools are for specific problems. Open the one that matches what you
  see.

## Fonts and Chinese typesetting

### 2.1 Apply Font Pairing 
Use it when you want to change which font goes with which across languages,
for example a different Chinese font to go with a Latin one. The import already
asked for pairings it needed; this is for changing them afterwards.

1. Open the translated document and double-click **2.1 Apply Font Pairing** in
   the Scripts panel.
2. A panel opens with the fonts the document uses. Set which font each one pairs
   with.
3. Click **Done**. A message says how many changes it made.

It changes the fonts directly on the text and creates no new paragraph or
character styles. The whole batch is one undo step.

### 2.2 Apply CJK Styles 
Use it when Chinese text needs Chinese line breaking and the other Chinese
typesetting settings.

1. Click into the text you want to set. With nothing selected, it works on the
   whole document.
2. Double-click **2.2 Apply CJK Styles**.
3. In the dialog, choose your language (it always starts at Simplified
   Chinese) and which cleanups to run, then click **OK**.

> **Line breaks you placed by hand**
The cleanup **Remove soft line breaks** is ticked every time and removes every
soft line break (Shift+Enter) in the **whole document**, even when you selected
one text frame. If you have placed line breaks by hand, for example after
running 2.2 once already, untick it.

It brings a ready-made Chinese paragraph style with its line-breaking and
typesetting settings into the document and applies it, and tells you clearly if
[those settings did not come through](#kinsoku-not-applied). It also protects the layout by itself:
text frames too short for a line of Chinese are made taller first, and the
layout is checked and repaired afterwards, so you do not need 3.1 and 3.2
around it. It is one undo step.

### 2.3 Set Selection Weight 
Use it when selected text needs to be a certain weight, such as bold, in the
fonts set up for your brand, even when it mixes Chinese and Latin text.

1. Select the text.
2. Double-click **2.3 Set Selection Weight**.
3. Pick the weight in the dialog and click **OK**.

The Chinese and the Latin parts of the selection each get the right font for
that weight. If it cannot finish, it changes nothing and
[says why](#weight-stopped). It is one undo step.

### 2.5 Repair Cluster GREP 
Use it when, in a document imported with an older version, punctuation between
Latin words (a curly apostrophe, for example) shows in the Chinese font.

1. Open the document.
2. Double-click **2.5 Repair Cluster GREP**. It asks nothing.

It updates the rules inside the document's generated paragraph styles that
decide which characters get the Latin font and which the Chinese font, then
refreshes the text. Running it again changes nothing. It is one undo step.
Documents imported with the current version do not need it.

### 2.6 Convert Underline to Rule 
Use it when a whole paragraph is underlined and the line breaks up: hidden
under Chinese characters, showing under Latin letters and digits.

1. Open the document.
2. Double-click **2.6 Convert Underline to Rule**. It asks nothing.
3. Read the summary it shows at the end.

For every paragraph whose visible text is fully underlined, it removes the
underline and draws a thin line under the paragraph instead, in the colour of
the underlined text. That line runs unbroken under both scripts. Paragraphs already
converted are skipped. It is one undo step.

## Protect the layout during big changes 
**3.1** and **3.2** are a pair. Run 3.1 just before a big change you make by
hand, such as a find and replace across the document or editing a paragraph
style, and 3.2 just after it. **2.2 Apply CJK Styles** and the import already
do this themselves.

### 3.1 Snapshot Before Apply 
Use it right before the big change.

1. Open the document and double-click **3.1 Snapshot Before Apply**.

It records the current state of the text so that 3.2 can restore it. It also
makes text frames taller where they are too short to hold a line of Chinese
text; left alone, those frames
[come back empty after the change](#frames-empty).

### 3.2 Repair After Apply 
Use it right after the big change, when you ran 3.1 before it.

1. Double-click **3.2 Repair After Apply**.

It reads what 3.1 recorded, repairs what the change disturbed, and writes a
report of what it checked.

## Next

[4 Later rounds](/folio/rounds): when the translation changes after you
adjusted the layout.

## Common problems

> **I closed the font pairing panel and nothing changed**
Closing the panel without clicking **Done** makes no changes. Run
**2.1 Apply Font Pairing** again and finish with **Done**.

> **Text frames came back empty after a big change**
<a id="frames-empty"></a>

Frames too short for a line of Chinese text empty out when the text is
recomposed. Undo the change, run **3.1 Snapshot Before Apply** (it makes those
frames taller first), make the change again, then run **3.2 Repair After Apply**.
2.2 Apply CJK Styles does this by itself.

> **2.3 stopped with a message**
<a id="weight-stopped"></a>

In rare or unclear cases it stops rather than guessing, and leaves the selection
as it was. Every stop is written to its log. The message says what to change.
The usual ones: select text with the Type tool, not a frame; select text that
uses one font for the Chinese and one for the Latin; install the font it names,
or pick a weight that is installed.

> **2.2 says Kinsoku (line breaking) was not applied**
<a id="kinsoku-not-applied"></a>

The ready-made Chinese style that comes with the scripts arrived without its
line-breaking rules, so lines may break in the wrong places. Paste the
[install line](/guide/install) again and choose **Repair**, which rewrites the
scripts' files, then run 2.2 again. If the message comes back, report it on
[GitHub](https://github.com/zxa24/creative-script-installer/issues).

> **Technical details**
<a id="apply-font-pairing-details"></a>**2.1 Apply Font Pairing**
(source `font_apply_panel.idjs`)

1. It scans the active document and collects the fonts in use, their weights,
   and how much text each one carries.
2. It opens a panel inside InDesign where you set the pairings.
3. On **Done**, it applies the pairing-driven font swaps as direct format
   overrides. It does **not** create paragraph or character styles to do it.
4. It reports how many swaps landed.

**Undo:** the whole batch is wrapped in one undo step; a single
<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>Z</kbd> reverts all of it.

<a id="apply-cjk-styles-details"></a>**2.2 Apply CJK Styles**
(source `cjk_style_apply.idjs`)

1. It asks which cleanup passes to run first. The dialog offers three, all on
   by default on every run (nothing is remembered): **Remove soft line breaks (Shift+Enter)**, **Collapse consecutive
   empty lines (spaces too)** and **Remove spaces between CJK and ASCII**. The
   cleanups always run on the whole document; only the style merge follows the
   selection. "Remove spaces" matches Han characters only. The language list is
   zh-CN, zh-HK, zh-TW, ja and ko and always starts at zh-CN. The import (1.2)
   never runs these cleanups.
2. It works on either the story containing your selection, or on every
   repairable story in the document.
3. It opens the bundled CJK (Chinese, Japanese and Korean) donor document,
   imports its text styles into your document (this brings in the Chinese
   composition settings, including the kinsoku line-breaking set) and applies the donor paragraph style.
4. It verifies that the donor style actually arrived with its CJK settings
   intact, and says so loudly if the import came through broken.

**Undo:** the import and apply are wrapped in one undo step.

<a id="set-selection-weight-details"></a>**2.3 Set Selection Weight**
(source `set_selection_weight.idjs`)

Select text, pick a target weight, and the script resolves that weight name to
a concrete (font, weight) pair via the brand configuration and applies it.

- If the document does not already have a character style for that weight, the
  script creates one on the fly.
- A **mixed Han + Latin selection is routed per script**, so each half gets the
  right family, full-width punctuation included.
- Existing paragraph-level overrides are left alone; only character-level
  overrides in the selection are cleared.

**Failure behaviour:** it fails loudly, never silently. Rare or ambiguous cases
exit with a message, and every exit is logged. If applying fails, the whole
change is rolled back as one unit rather than leaving the selection half
changed.

<a id="repair-cluster-grep-details"></a>**2.5 Repair Cluster GREP**
(source `repair_cluster_grep.idjs`)

The problem it fixes: in a bilingual document built with the older rule set,
neutral punctuation (a curly apostrophe, U+2019, for instance) sitting between
Latin letters inside a Chinese-cluster document was left out of the Latin GREP,
so it stayed orphaned on the full-width CJK font.

This script rewrites the `grepExpression` of every managed cluster paragraph
style's nested Latin and CJK GREP rules to the current, context-aware patterns,
then recomposes so already-orphaned marks are re-routed.

- **It is a repair for documents already built with the old rules.** New imports
  get the current rules from the pipeline; they do not need this.
- **It is idempotent.** Re-running it rewrites nothing.
- **Undo:** one undo step for the whole run.

<a id="convert-underline-to-rule-details"></a>**2.6 Convert Underline to Rule**
(source `convert_underline_to_rule.idjs`)

It scans every paragraph in every story and finds the ones where **100% of the
visible characters** carry character-level `underline = true`. For each, it
removes the character-level underline and puts a paragraph-level rule below
instead: 0.5pt, text width, coloured from the majority fill colour of the
underlined characters.

**Why:** a character-level underline tracks each glyph's own baseline. CJK
glyphs hide the line under their body while Latin characters and digits expose
it, so a mixed line gets a half-drawn underline. A paragraph rule sits at the
paragraph baseline and stays continuous across both scripts.

- It lives outside the import pipeline on purpose, so the import stays
  format-neutral and **you** decide when to apply this visual change.
- **It is idempotent.** Paragraphs already converted are skipped.
- **It writes** a log to `<document folder>/convert_underline_to_rule_<timestamp>.log`.

<a id="snapshot-before-apply-details"></a>**3.1 Snapshot Before Apply**
(source `snapshot_before_apply.idjs`; pairs with 3.2)

Run it **before** any bulk text replacement or CJK style application. It:

1. Expands geometry-split frames that are too short to hold a line of CJK text.
   Left alone, those frames come back empty after recomposition.
2. Captures a "before" snapshot of every repairable story.
3. Saves that snapshot twice: once as `before_snapshot_latest.json` and once
   as `<document name>_before_snapshot.json`.

3.2 Repair After Apply reads that file and uses it as the target state to
restore.

<a id="repair-after-apply-details"></a>**3.2 Repair After Apply**
(source `repair_after_apply.idjs`; pairs with 3.1)

Reads the snapshot from 3.1, repairs what the bulk change disturbed, and writes
an acceptance report. The intended sequence is:

1. 3.1 Snapshot Before Apply: save the "before" snapshot and expand the short
   frames.
2. Do the bulk change: text replacement, CJK style import, whatever it is.
3. 3.2 Repair After Apply: read the snapshot, repair, and report.

---

<!-- page: folio/rounds.md -->
# Later rounds

Source: https://zxa24.github.io/creative-script-installer/folio/rounds

Summary: Stage 4 for the designer. When the client or reviewer changes the translation after you adjusted the layout, update the translated document you adjusted instead of starting again, and use 3.4 Highlight Translation Changes to mark every changed character without touching the text.

# Later rounds

Stage 4 of [Translate a layout: for designers](/folio/designer). Use this page
when the client or reviewer changes the translation after you have adjusted the
layout, and to see, or show a reviewer, exactly what changed since the last
round.

These are free InDesign scripts from Creative Script Kit. You install them
once with one line ([Install](/guide/install)) and find them in the Scripts
panel under **User → indesign-toolkit-stable**
([where to find the scripts](/guide/install#where-to-find-the-scripts)).

## The next round of changes 
Do **not** start again from the original. Update the translated document
instead:

1. **Open your `.translated.indd`** (the one you adjusted) and capture a
   baseline before you change anything. Double-click
   **3.4 Highlight Translation Changes**, choose **Capture baseline** and click
   **OK**. Nothing visible changes. Then run
   **1.1 Export Translation Package** on it and send the new zip to the
   translator.
2. **The translator edits the existing text** in the web app. Paragraphs they do
   not touch stay exactly as they are.
3. **Open the same `.translated.indd`** and run
   **1.2 Import Translation Package** with the new zip. It updates this document
   itself; no new copy is made. A copy of the previous version is saved first in
   **script_outputs → backup** (if that copy fails, see
   [The import says the safety backup could not be made](/folio/export-import#backup-failed)).
4. **Mark and check the paragraphs that changed.** Run
   **3.4 Highlight Translation Changes** again, choose **Highlight changes**,
   pick the starting point you saved from the list, and click **OK**. Tick
   **Ignore whitespace differences** if only the wording matters to you. Your
   other adjustments stay, but inside a changed paragraph, hand adjustments
   such as no-break, tracking and line breaks are cleared. Redo them there.
5. **Delete the highlight layer before you export the final PDF.** In the
   Layers panel, delete the layer named **_T_translation_highlights**. The
   marks are ordinary page items, so otherwise they print in it.

> **Do not import a later round into the original**
<a id="next-round-warning"></a>That starts over and replaces the
`.translated.indd` you adjusted, with no backup and no warning. All your layout
work in it is lost.

## 3.4 Highlight Translation Changes 
Use it when you need the edited text marked, for example in a PDF that goes back
to the reviewer. It has two choices: **Capture baseline** saves the text as it
stands, and **Highlight changes** marks what changed since a baseline you saved.

- Capture a baseline before you change anything: right after the first
  import, and again at the start of each later round (step 1 above). Edits
  made before you capture it cannot be marked later.
- Changed text gets a yellow box, and a place where text was deleted gets a red
  mark. The marks sit on their own layer, behind the text; the text itself is
  not changed in any way.
- Each new **Highlight changes** run clears the old marks first, so they never
  pile up.
- To remove the marks when you no longer need them, delete the layer named
  **_T_translation_highlights** in the Layers panel. The marks are ordinary
  page items, so they show in a PDF you export.

## Next

[5 Sister documents](/folio/sister-documents): copy tuned paragraph-style
settings to a sister document.

## Common problems

> **Highlight changes is not available**
There is no starting point yet. Run it once with **Capture baseline** first.

> **Will adding or removing paragraphs make everything light up?**
No. When paragraphs have moved, it matches each one by its content instead of
its position, so only the real changes are marked.

> **Spaces and line breaks are marked too**
That is the default. Run **Highlight changes** again with
**Ignore whitespace differences** ticked.

> **Technical details**
<a id="highlight-translation-changes-details"></a>**3.4 Highlight Translation Changes**
(source `track_translation_changes.idjs`)

The highlight is a **separate layer of yellow rectangles drawn behind the
text**. It has zero effect on the text's own properties: underlines, character
styles and everything else are untouched.

From the Scripts panel the dialog offers **Capture baseline** (the `rebaseline`
mode below) and **Highlight changes** (a diff against the chosen baseline). The
modes are how automation drives it:

| Mode | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `auto` (default) | **First run:** captures a baseline, with no visible change to the document. **Later runs:** diffs every paragraph against the baseline character by character and marks the changed substrings. It always clears the previous overlay first, so stale marks never pile up. |
| `clear` | Deletes the highlight layer and everything on it. The baseline file is kept. |
| `rebaseline` | Clears the overlay, then re-captures the baseline as the new ground truth. |

**Options**

- **Ignore whitespace:** suppresses highlights whose inserted or deleted
  characters are pure whitespace (space, tab, newline, non-breaking space,
  ideographic space). **Off by default**; turn it on when you only care about
  content edits and want post-translation whitespace shuffling ignored.
- **Baseline file:** pick which baseline JSON to diff against, either from the
  dropdown of files in the baselines folder or by giving an arbitrary path.
  Capture mode ignores this and always writes a fresh timestamped file.

Baselines are saved in `<document folder>/script_outputs/baseline_snapshots/`.

**Surviving structural edits**

The baseline is keyed positionally first, by story and paragraph index, which
is the fast path when the structure has not changed. When a paragraph's text
turns out to be wildly different from the baseline entry at that position (a
sign that paragraphs were added or removed and indices have shifted), it falls
back to matching on a content fingerprint. That is what keeps a document from
lighting up with false positives after "N paragraphs added between capture and
diff".

For what the import does in a later round (in-place update, the backup, what
is cleared in changed paragraphs), see the technical details of
[1.2 Import Translation Package](/folio/export-import#import-translation-package).

---

<!-- page: folio/sister-documents.md -->
# Sister documents

Source: https://zxa24.github.io/creative-script-installer/folio/sister-documents

Summary: Copy tuned paragraph-style settings from one InDesign document to a sister document without redoing them by hand. 4.1 Export Brand Preset saves the settings; 4.2 Apply Brand Preset applies them. Fonts are never changed.

# Sister documents

Stage 5 of [Translate a layout: for designers](/folio/designer). Use this page
when you tuned the paragraph styles of one document over several rounds and a
sister document needs to match, without redoing the work by hand.

These are free InDesign scripts from Creative Script Kit. You install them
once with one line ([Install](/guide/install)) and find them in the Scripts
panel under **User → indesign-toolkit-stable**
([where to find the scripts](/guide/install#where-to-find-the-scripts)).

A sister document is another document in the same family as the one you
tuned, for example the same fact sheet for a different product, laid out with
the same styles.

**4.1** saves the settings from the document you tuned. **4.2** applies them to
the sister document. Both work on the paragraph styles that Folio's import or
[**2.4 Reorganize Styles**](/folio/before-export#reorganize-styles) created, and
neither ever changes fonts. To check
that a document has them, open the Paragraph Styles panel: their names start
with `_T_p_`.

## 4.1 Export Brand Preset 
Use it in the document whose paragraph styles you have tuned.

1. Save the document. The settings file is written next to it.
2. Double-click **4.1 Export Brand Preset** in the Scripts panel. It asks
   nothing.

It saves each style's size, line spacing, indents, space before and after,
alignment, colour and rules into a settings file (a brand preset) named
`brand_style_preset.json`. If a brand configuration file next to the document
names the brand, the brand name goes in front:
`<brand>_brand_style_preset.json`. It only reads the document and changes
nothing in it.

## 4.2 Apply Brand Preset 
Use it in the sister document that should match.

1. Save the sister document, and make sure the preset file from 4.1 is in the
   same folder. If the two documents share a folder, it already is. 4.2 looks
   in its own document's folder for a file whose name ends in
   `_brand_style_preset.json`, and uses `brand_style_preset.json` only if there
   is none. If there are several, it takes the one for this document's brand,
   or else the newest, and says so in its log. Keep only the one you want in
   that folder.
2. Double-click **4.2 Apply Brand Preset**. It asks nothing.
3. Check its report in the **log** folder inside **script_outputs**, next to
   the document. If some settings did not carry over, see
   [below](#settings-not-carried).

It updates the matching paragraph styles with the saved settings. Fonts are
never touched. It is one undo step.

Hand changes in the sister document are kept for size, line spacing, indents,
keep options, alignment and composer, and listed in the report. Space before
and after, colour and rules are always overwritten with the preset's values.

## Common problems

> **4.2 says no preset was found**
The preset file is not in the sister document's folder, or the document has
never been saved. Copy the file from the first document's folder and run it
again. Nothing was changed.

> **Some settings did not carry over**
<a id="settings-not-carried"></a>

A size, line spacing, indent, keep option, alignment or composer that someone
changed by hand in the sister document is kept and listed as kept local. Space
before and after, colour and rules are always written; a colour or rule that
did not take is listed as failed. It never hides either case.

> **The report says the styles were reused, but not everything changed**
"Reused" only means a style found its match. Read it together with the applied
rate, the kept local count and the failed count.

> **Technical details**
<a id="export-brand-preset-details"></a>**4.1 Export Brand Preset**
(source `export_brand_style_preset.idjs`)

It reads the active document's `_T_p_*` paragraph-style definitions and writes
their geometry into a preset file:

- point size and leading
- indents and space before / space after
- justification and composer
- fill colour
- rules above and below

**It is read-only on the document.** It builds a preset *from* the styles; it
does not modify them. The one undo-block it opens exists only to hold a
consistent points-based measurement context while reading numbers, and to give
a clean single-undo boundary; nothing is written to the document.

**Output:** next to the saved `.indd`, plus a summary log. The file is
`<brand>_brand_style_preset.json` when a `<document name>_brand_config.json` or
`brand_config.json` beside the document gives a brand name, otherwise
`brand_style_preset.json`.

<a id="apply-brand-preset-details"></a>**4.2 Apply Brand Preset**
(source `apply_brand_style_preset.idjs`)

It loads a `brand_style_preset.json` captured by 4.1 and writes its tuned
geometry onto the active document's matching `_T_p_*` paragraph-style
**definitions**.

**It never touches fonts.** `appliedFont` and `fontStyle` are out of scope, by
design.

**How it finds the preset**

1. An explicitly given path, used verbatim.
2. Otherwise, `<saved document folder>/*_brand_style_preset.json`. With
   several matches it prefers the one named for this document's brand, then
   the newest by modification date, and logs the choice as ambiguous.
3. Otherwise, `<saved document folder>/brand_style_preset.json`.
4. If none of these turns one up, it reports "no preset found" and exits
   cleanly; that is not treated as an error.

**What happens when the target document disagrees**

Conflicts are resolved per dimension, not per style.

**Protected dimensions** (point size, leading, indents, keep options,
justification, composer) are reconciled three ways against what was last
applied and what the style was created with:

| The live value is… | Result |
| --- | --- |
| the same as what was last applied | safe to update: take the preset's value |
| the same as the creation baseline (never touched locally) | take the preset's value |
| different from both (someone tuned it locally) | **keep the local value** and report it |

**Always-apply dimensions** (space before / space after, fill colour, rules
above and below) have no reconstructable creation baseline, so the preset's
value is always written. The colour and rule writes are then **read back and
verified**, and reported as applied-OK or applied-FAILED. A write that silently
did not land is reported, not swallowed.

All of it is applied in one undo step. The coverage report is written to the
log folder (`script_outputs/log/`).

**Reading the report**

The headline number is **reuse rate**: matched styles divided by total. A style
counts as matched even if one of its dimensions was kept local or failed to
apply.

Three separate counts sit next to it so "reuse" is never misread as "everything
transferred":

- **applied rate**
- **kept-local count**
- **applied-failed count**

Read all four together.

---

<!-- page: tools/index.md -->
# More tools

Source: https://zxa24.github.io/creative-script-installer/tools/

Summary: Tools in Creative Script Kit that are not part of the translation workflow. In InDesign, 3.5 Save and Reveal saves the document and opens its folder. In Illustrator, five tools for everyday chores, Unembed All Images, Export Artboard PDFs, Export Small PDF, Replace Fonts, and CJK Composer and Mojikumi, with when to use each and what to answer.

# More tools

These tools are not part of the translation workflow: each one does an
everyday job on its own. You install them with the other scripts, with one line
([Install](/guide/install)).

## InDesign 
Find it in the Scripts panel under **User → indesign-toolkit-stable**
([where to find the scripts](/guide/install#where-to-find-the-scripts)).

### 3.5 Save and Reveal 
Use it when you want to save the document and open the folder it is in.

1. Double-click **3.5 Save and Reveal** in the Scripts panel.
2. If the document has unsaved changes, it asks whether to save it. For a
   document that has never been saved, saying yes opens the Save As dialog.

It saves only when you say yes, then opens the document's folder in Explorer or
Finder.

## Illustrator 
Five small tools for everyday chores in Illustrator, found under
**File → Scripts → illustrator-toolkit-stable**.

### Unembed All Images 
Use it when a file has images embedded in it and you want them as separate,
linked files, or when you want to clear out broken links.

1. Save the document, then choose
   **File → Scripts → illustrator-toolkit-stable → Unembed All Images**.
2. The *Asset Management* window shows how many embedded images and broken
   links it found. Tick what you want: export the embedded images and relink
   them, remove the broken links, or both. **Change...** picks another output
   folder.
3. Click **Run** and read the summary.

It writes one file per embedded image into a new **Linked_assets** folder next
to the document (or **Linked_assets_1**, and so on, if that name is taken), and
links the artwork to those files.

### Export Artboard PDFs 
Use it when each artboard needs to be its own PDF.

1. Save the document, then choose
   **File → Scripts → illustrator-toolkit-stable → Export Artboard PDFs**.
2. If the document has broken links, choose what to do with them: relink them
   from a folder, skip them during export, delete them from the document, or
   cancel.
3. In *Export Artboards as PDF*, tick **PDF**, **Print PDF** (with bleed) or
   **.ai File**, pick a PDF preset, and click **Export**.

It writes one file per artboard, named after the artboard, into a new folder
next to the document whose name ends in `_export`, then opens that folder. To
change the file names, rename the artboards in the Artboards panel first.

### Export Small PDF 
Use it to finish a job in one click: export the smallest PDF, the largest PDF,
save the document and package it, in any combination.

1. Save the document, then choose
   **File → Scripts → illustrator-toolkit-stable → Export Small PDF**.
2. In *Quick Actions*, tick what you want: **Export smallest PDF** (ticked by
   default), **Export largest PDF**, **Save document**, **Package**.
3. Click **OK**.

The PDFs go next to the document as `<name>_smallest.pdf` and
`<name>_highquality.pdf` (a number is added if the file exists), and the
folder opens. **Package** opens Illustrator's own Package dialog at the end.

> **Save first**
To export, it closes your document and opens it again from disk. Changes you
have not saved are not kept in the `.ai` file, so save first or tick
**Save document**.

### Replace Fonts 
Use it when one font has to be replaced by another across a whole file or a
selection.

1. Choose **File → Scripts → illustrator-toolkit-stable → Replace Fonts**.
2. Click **+ Add** and pick a *From* font and a *To* font for each row. Type
   in **Filter** and click **Search** to narrow the font lists.
3. Under **Scope**, choose **Whole document** or **Selection only**, then
   click **Replace**.

It changes the fonts in the document and reports how many characters it
replaced. **Save rules** and **Load rules** keep a list of pairs for next time.
To reverse it, use **Edit → Undo**.

### CJK Composer and Mojikumi 
Use it when Chinese or Japanese text needs CJK (Chinese, Japanese and Korean)
typesetting: the CJK composer, a Mojikumi set (spacing rules between
characters) and a Kinsoku set (rules for which characters may not start or end
a line).

1. Select the text frames to work on, or select nothing to work on every text
   frame.
2. Choose
   **File → Scripts → illustrator-toolkit-stable → CJK Composer and Mojikumi**.
3. If something is selected, it asks a question: **OK** works on the selected
   text frames only. If it finds spaces between CJK and Latin text, it lists
   them: **OK** removes them, **Cancel** keeps them.

> **Cancel does not stop the script**
In the first question, **Cancel does not stop the script**. It means "work on
every text frame in the document". There is no way to stop it at that
question. To work on your selection only, click **OK**; to reverse a run, use
**Edit → Undo**.

It sets the composer, Mojikumi and Kinsoku on each paragraph, adds a little
space where CJK text meets Latin letters or digits, and tightens full-width
punctuation in text frames that overflow. Locked and hidden text frames are
skipped. A summary lists what it set.

## Common problems

> **An Illustrator tool says "No document open"**
Every Illustrator tool needs an open document. Open the file and run it again.

> **An Illustrator tool asks me to save first**
Unembed All Images, Export Artboard PDFs and Export Small PDF write files next
to the document, so it must have been saved once. Save it and run the tool
again.

> **I lost changes after Export Small PDF**
It closes the document and opens it again from disk to export. Anything not
saved before that is not in the `.ai` file. Next time, save first or tick
**Save document**.

> **Replace Fonts says nothing is selected**
**Scope** is set to **Selection only**. Select a text frame or group with the
Selection tool, or select text with the Type tool, and run it again. Or choose
**Whole document**.

> **Replace Fonts says the same From font appears in more than one row**
Each *From* font can appear in one row only. Remove or merge the duplicate
rows and click **Replace** again.

> **The bleed I typed in Export Artboard PDFs is gone next time**
The bleed values are stored in the document. Save the document after the
export to keep them.

> **The summary says Mojikumi or Kinsoku "(not set / not found)"**
The document has no Mojikumi or Kinsoku set to use, so that part was skipped.
The other settings were still applied.

> **Technical details**
Most people never need to change these.

<a id="save-and-reveal-details"></a>**3.5 Save and Reveal**
(source `save_and_reveal.idjs`)

Offers to save the active document if it has unsaved changes, then opens its
folder in the system file browser. A small convenience: run it, answer the save
prompt if one appears, and the document's folder opens in Explorer or Finder.

<a id="illustrator-details"></a>**Illustrator tools: undo and files.** Changes
to the document go through Illustrator's own undo. Files a tool writes (PDFs,
images, `.ai` copies) stay on disk; Undo does not remove them. All five tools
stop with a message when no document is open.

**Unembed All Images**

The default output folder is `<document folder>/Linked_assets`, or
`Linked_assets_<n>` if that folder exists. If there is nothing embedded and no
broken link, it says so and stops.

**Export Artboard PDFs**

- Each artboard is exported by duplicating it into a new document, so nothing
  from the other artboards gets in.
- PDF presets offered: `[Smallest File Size]`, `[High Quality Print]`,
  `[Press Quality]`, `[PDF/X-1a:2001]`, `[PDF/X-4:2008]`.
- Output folder: `<document folder>/<YYYYMMDD>_<HHMM>_export`. Files:
  `<artboard>.pdf`, `<artboard>_print.pdf` (with marks and bleeds) and
  `<artboard>.ai`. A log is saved in the same folder.
- Bleed units: mm, pt, in or px (default 0.125 in). The values are stored in a
  hidden page item named `__ExportArtboardPDFs__`.

**Export Small PDF**

The smallest PDF uses the `[Smallest File Size]` preset and the largest uses
`[High Quality Print]`. **Save document** runs first, then the PDFs, then
**Package** (`File → Package`).

**Replace Fonts**

Options in the window: **List all fonts in the From menu** (off by default;
otherwise only the fonts in use), **Grow frames that overset after replacing**
(on by default; it reports how many it fixed and how many still overflow) and
**Halfwidth characters only (Latin, digits, punctuation)** (off by default),
which leaves CJK text on its current font.

**CJK Composer and Mojikumi: settings at the top of the script**

The `.jsx` file in the **illustrator-toolkit-stable** folder starts with a
block of settings. An update replaces the file, so edits there do not survive
an update.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `COMPOSER_MODE` | `"paragraph"` | Every-line composer; `"single"` for the single-line composer. |
| `SET_MOJIKUMI`, `SET_KINSOKU` | `true` | Whether to set a Mojikumi and a Kinsoku set. |
| `MOJIKUMI_NAME`, `KINSOKU_NAME` | `""` | The set to use, by name. Empty: the first set whose name contains 简体, 繁体, 中文, Chinese, JIS, 日本 or Japanese, or else the first set the document has. |
| `ENABLE_BURASAGARI`, `BURASAGARI_MODE` | `true`, Standard | Hanging punctuation at the line end. |
| `ENABLE_BUNRIKINSHI` | `true` | Keeps certain character pairs from being split. |
| `TSUME_PERCENT` | `null` | Tightens every character by this percentage; `null` leaves it alone. |
| `ENABLE_PUNCTUATION_SQUEEZE`, `PUNCTUATION_TSUME` | `true`, `50` | Tightens full-width punctuation, only in area text frames that overflow. |
| `ENABLE_CJK_LATIN_SPACING`, `CJK_LATIN_AKI` | `true`, `25` | Space where CJK text meets Latin letters or digits, as a percentage of a full-width character. |
| `ENABLE_REMOVE_CJK_LATIN_SPACES` | `true` | Offers to remove typed spaces between CJK and Latin text. |

Whether it works on the selection or the whole document is not a setting: it
comes from the first question, and with nothing selected it always works on
every text frame.

---

# All scripts

Summary: Every script in Creative Script Kit. The numbered InDesign scripts in Scripts panel order and the five Illustrator scripts, each with one line on what it is for and a link to where it is explained.

The numbers group the InDesign scripts by kind; they are not the order you run
them in. For the order, see [For designers](/folio/designer).
